topics: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control

questions.question_text: Which of the following microorganisms is classified as a bacterium?

choices.text: Plasmodium falciparum
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Human immunodeficiency virus
Candida albicans

questions.rationale: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a bacterium that causes tuberculosis. Plasmodium is a protozoan parasite, HIV is a virus, and Candida is a fungus.

questions.question_text: Which characteristic distinguishes viruses from bacteria?

choices.text: Viruses reproduce independently in nutrient media
Viruses require living host cells for replication
Viruses possess a cellular nucleus
Viruses are always larger than bacteria

questions.rationale: Viruses are obligate intracellular agents and depend on host-cell machinery to replicate. Bacteria are cellular organisms that can reproduce independently under suitable conditions.

questions.question_text: Which microorganism causes malaria?

choices.text: Salmonella Typhi
Plasmodium species
Vibrio cholerae
Hepatitis B virus

questions.rationale: Malaria is caused by protozoan parasites belonging to the genus Plasmodium. In Ghana, Plasmodium falciparum is the predominant species responsible for severe malaria.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a fungal pathogen?

choices.text: Candida albicans
Escherichia coli
Hepatitis B virus
Plasmodium falciparum

questions.rationale: Candida albicans is a yeast belonging to the kingdom Fungi and can cause infections such as oral and vaginal candidiasis. Escherichia coli is a bacterium, while hepatitis B virus and Plasmodium are different types of infectious agents.

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of the chain of infection?

choices.text: Infectious agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, susceptible host
Reservoir, susceptible host, infectious agent, portal of entry, portal of exit, transmission
Portal of entry, infectious agent, reservoir, susceptible host, portal of exit, transmission
Infectious agent, portal of entry, portal of exit, reservoir, transmission, susceptible host

questions.rationale: The six links are the infectious agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry and susceptible host. Infection prevention aims to interrupt one or more of these links.

questions.question_text: In the chain of infection, what is a reservoir?

choices.text: The route through which microorganisms enter a host
The place where an infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
The process by which an infection is diagnosed
The medication used to destroy microorganisms

questions.rationale: A reservoir is the natural habitat in which an infectious agent lives, grows or multiplies. Examples include humans, animals, water, soil and contaminated materials.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of hand hygiene in healthcare settings?

choices.text: To remove visible stains from healthcare workers' hands only
To prevent the transmission of microorganisms
To replace the use of personal protective equipment
To sterilize the hands permanently

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene reduces transient microorganisms and helps prevent cross-transmission between patients, healthcare workers and the environment. It is a fundamental component of standard precautions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a standard precaution that should be applied to every patient?

choices.text: Using gloves only when a patient is known to have HIV
Performing hand hygiene according to recommended indications
Isolating every patient in a separate room
Administering antibiotics before every procedure

questions.rationale: Standard precautions apply to all patients, regardless of their suspected or confirmed infection status. Hand hygiene is required at appropriate moments during patient care.

questions.question_text: Which item of personal protective equipment primarily protects the eyes from splashes of potentially infectious material?

choices.text: Disposable apron
Protective goggles
Surgical cap
Shoe cover

questions.rationale: Protective goggles provide a barrier against splashes reaching the eyes. Face shields may also protect the eyes and face when splash exposure is anticipated.

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between sterilization and disinfection?

choices.text: Sterilization destroys all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores, while disinfection reduces or eliminates many pathogenic microorganisms
Disinfection always destroys bacterial spores, while sterilization destroys only viruses
Sterilization is used only for floors, while disinfection is used only for surgical instruments
Both processes have exactly the same meaning

questions.rationale: Sterilization eliminates all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores, when properly performed. Disinfection reduces or eliminates many pathogenic microorganisms but does not necessarily destroy bacterial spores.

questions.question_text: A healthcare-associated infection is best described as an infection that:

choices.text: Is always present before a patient enters a health facility
Is acquired during the process of receiving healthcare and was not present or incubating at the time of care
Occurs only among healthcare workers
Can only be caused by viruses

questions.rationale: Healthcare-associated infections are linked to the provision of healthcare and were not present or incubating when the relevant care began. They can affect patients and healthcare workers and may be caused by bacteria, viruses or fungi.

questions.question_text: Which bacterium is responsible for typhoid fever?

choices.text: Vibrio cholerae
Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi
Mycobacterium leprae
Clostridium tetani

questions.rationale: Typhoid fever is caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi. It is commonly transmitted through food or water contaminated with faeces from an infected person or carrier.

questions.question_text: Which organism causes cholera?

choices.text: Vibrio cholerae
Salmonella Typhi
Plasmodium falciparum
Streptococcus pneumoniae

questions.rationale: Cholera is an acute diarrhoeal disease caused by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae, particularly serogroups O1 and O139. It spreads mainly through ingestion of contaminated food or water.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of vaccination?

choices.text: To produce immunity against specific infectious diseases
To treat all existing bacterial infections
To replace personal hygiene practices
To guarantee that a vaccinated person will never become ill

questions.rationale: Vaccination stimulates the immune system to develop protection against specific pathogens or their toxins. It reduces the risk of disease and severe complications but does not guarantee complete protection in every individual.

questions.question_text: What does antimicrobial resistance mean?

choices.text: The ability of the human body to destroy every microorganism
The ability of microorganisms to survive or grow despite exposure to medicines that would normally inhibit or kill them
The inability of antibiotics to treat viral infections
The development of immunity after vaccination

questions.rationale: Antimicrobial resistance occurs when microorganisms develop mechanisms that reduce their susceptibility to antimicrobial medicines. Resistant infections can become more difficult to treat and may require alternative medicines.

questions.question_text: Which waste category should used needles and other contaminated sharps be placed in?

choices.text: General domestic waste
A designated puncture-resistant sharps container
An ordinary paper waste basket
An open plastic bag

questions.rationale: Used needles and other sharps must be discarded immediately into a designated puncture-resistant sharps container. This reduces needlestick injuries and exposure to blood-borne pathogens.

questions.question_text: Which route is primarily responsible for the transmission of pulmonary tuberculosis?

choices.text: Inhalation of infectious airborne particles released by a person with infectious pulmonary or laryngeal TB
Sharing eating utensils with an infected person
Mosquito bites
Contact with contaminated soil through intact skin

questions.rationale: Pulmonary tuberculosis is transmitted through the air when a person with infectious pulmonary or laryngeal TB releases infectious particles, particularly while coughing or speaking. Prolonged or repeated exposure in poorly ventilated spaces increases the risk of transmission.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is about to perform a wound dressing at a CHPS compound. The nurse's hands are visibly soiled with blood. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Apply alcohol-based hand rub over the blood
Wash the hands with soap and running water
Put on gloves without cleaning the hands
Wipe the hands on a clean towel

questions.rationale: Hands visibly soiled with blood or other body fluids should be washed with soap and running water. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene and should be put on after hand hygiene has been performed.

questions.question_text: After examining a patient with suspected cholera, a nurse is preparing to attend to another patient. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Change gloves only and immediately attend to the next patient
Perform hand hygiene and use clean gloves when indicated for the next patient's care
Wear the same apron and gloves for both patients
Avoid hand hygiene because the nurse did not touch blood

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene must be performed after patient contact and after removing gloves. Gloves must be changed between patients, and appropriate protective clothing should be changed if contaminated.

questions.question_text: A nurse is assisting with a procedure likely to produce splashes of blood and body fluids. Which combination of PPE provides the most appropriate protection?

choices.text: Gloves only
Gloves, gown or apron, mask and eye or face protection
Surgical cap and shoe covers only
Apron only

questions.rationale: The anticipated exposure requires protection for the hands, clothing, respiratory mucosa and eyes. PPE should be selected according to the risk assessment of the procedure.

questions.question_text: A nurse has completed the care of a patient under contact precautions. Which action should be performed when removing contaminated gloves?

choices.text: Touch the outside of the gloves with bare fingers
Remove the gloves without touching their contaminated outer surfaces with bare skin
Wash the gloves while wearing them for reuse
Place the gloves in a pocket for later disposal

questions.rationale: Gloves should be removed carefully to avoid contaminating the hands with their outer surfaces. They should be discarded appropriately, followed by hand hygiene.

questions.question_text: A surgical instrument has been used on a patient and is intended for another invasive procedure. Which processing method is required before reuse?

choices.text: Rinsing with clean water only
Sterilization after appropriate cleaning and preparation
Wiping with a dry cloth
Low-level disinfection only

questions.rationale: Critical instruments that enter sterile tissue or the vascular system must be sterilized before reuse. Thorough cleaning is necessary before sterilization because organic material can interfere with the process.

questions.question_text: A CHPS nurse is preparing a reusable thermometer for use on another patient. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use it immediately because thermometers do not transmit infection
Clean and disinfect it according to the manufacturer's instructions and facility protocol
Immerse it in any chemical solution for several hours
Wipe it with a dry cloth only

questions.rationale: Reusable patient-care equipment must be appropriately cleaned and disinfected between patients. The selected product and contact time should be compatible with the equipment and the manufacturer's instructions.

questions.question_text: A patient develops redness, pain and discharge from a surgical wound several days after an operation in a district hospital. What should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: A surgical site infection
A vaccine reaction
A normal stage of wound healing in every patient
A fungal infection of the respiratory tract

questions.rationale: Increasing redness, pain and purulent discharge from a surgical wound are suggestive of a surgical site infection. The patient requires clinical assessment, appropriate documentation and management according to facility protocol.

questions.question_text: A nurse notices that several patients in a ward have developed diarrhoea after receiving care in the same facility. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Ignore the cases because diarrhoea is common
Report the suspected cluster promptly to the facility infection prevention and control team
Give all affected patients antibiotics without assessment
Discharge the patients immediately without documentation

questions.rationale: A cluster of similar infections may indicate a healthcare-associated outbreak requiring investigation. Prompt reporting supports early case identification, infection control measures and appropriate laboratory investigation.

questions.question_text: A child attending a CHPS compound presents with fever, chills, headache and vomiting. Malaria is suspected. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Start antimalarial treatment without testing in every case
Perform a malaria rapid diagnostic test or microscopy according to the applicable protocol
Assume the child has typhoid fever and prescribe antibiotics
Advise the caregiver to wait several days before seeking care

questions.rationale: Suspected malaria should be assessed using a recommended parasitological test, such as a rapid diagnostic test or microscopy. A positive result should be interpreted alongside the clinical assessment, and severe illness requires urgent management or referral.

questions.question_text: A patient at a district hospital has prolonged fever, abdominal discomfort and diarrhoea after drinking untreated water. Typhoid fever is suspected. Which investigation is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis where available?

choices.text: Blood culture
Skin scraping
Sputum acid-fast bacilli test
Malaria rapid diagnostic test only

questions.rationale: Blood culture is an important diagnostic method for identifying Salmonella Typhi, particularly before antibiotics are started. Clinical features alone cannot reliably distinguish typhoid fever from other causes of prolonged fever.

questions.question_text: A patient presents at a health facility with profuse watery diarrhoea, vomiting and signs of severe dehydration during a suspected cholera outbreak. What is the priority nursing action?

choices.text: Delay treatment until the laboratory result is available
Initiate urgent rehydration according to the severe dehydration protocol and arrange immediate clinical management
Give antidiarrhoeal medication and send the patient home
Restrict all oral and intravenous fluids

questions.rationale: Severe dehydration from suspected cholera is a medical emergency requiring immediate rehydration, commonly with intravenous fluids under the appropriate protocol. Treatment should not be delayed while awaiting laboratory confirmation.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse identifies a person with a persistent cough lasting more than two weeks, weight loss and night sweats. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Treat the person for malaria without further assessment
Arrange prompt TB screening and diagnostic evaluation through the appropriate service
Advise the person to avoid all health facilities
Give antibiotics for a common cold and close the case

questions.rationale: A persistent cough with weight loss and night sweats raises suspicion of tuberculosis and requires prompt assessment. The nurse should facilitate appropriate sputum-based or other recommended diagnostic testing and apply respiratory infection control measures.

questions.question_text: A patient newly diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis attends a CHPS compound for follow-up. Which advice is most appropriate to reduce transmission at home?

choices.text: Keep all windows closed to prevent dust from entering
Improve ventilation, practise cough etiquette and follow the prescribed TB treatment
Share sleeping space in a poorly ventilated room with household members
Stop treatment once the cough improves

questions.rationale: Good ventilation and cough etiquette reduce the concentration and spread of infectious airborne particles. Completing the prescribed TB regimen is essential for successful treatment and reducing the risk of drug resistance.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman attends antenatal care and is found to have a positive HIV test result following the recommended testing process. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Disclose her status to all members of the community
Link her promptly to HIV care and prevention of mother-to-child transmission services
Advise her to discontinue antenatal care
Tell her that transmission to the baby is inevitable

questions.rationale: Prompt linkage to HIV treatment and prevention of mother-to-child transmission services reduces the risk of HIV transmission to the infant. Counselling and management must respect confidentiality and national clinical guidance.

questions.question_text: A nurse sustains a needlestick injury from a needle recently used on a patient whose HIV status is unknown. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Squeeze the wound forcefully and apply bleach
Wash the affected area immediately with soap and running water
Ignore the injury if there is no visible bleeding
Wait until symptoms of HIV appear before reporting

questions.rationale: The exposed area should be washed promptly with soap and running water without squeezing or applying caustic substances. The exposure must be reported immediately for risk assessment, appropriate testing and consideration of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis as soon as possible.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is educating a household about preventing hepatitis B transmission. Which advice is correct?

choices.text: Avoid sharing razors and toothbrushes and ensure eligible household members are vaccinated
Share needles only with close relatives
Avoid drinking boiled water
Use antibiotics regularly to prevent hepatitis B

questions.rationale: Hepatitis B can be transmitted through infected blood and certain body fluids, including through shared contaminated sharp instruments. Vaccination and avoiding the sharing of razors, toothbrushes and needles are important preventive measures.

questions.question_text: A caregiver brings an infant to a CHPS compound for routine immunization. The infant has a mild runny nose but is active and feeding normally. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Automatically postpone all vaccines for one month
Assess the infant and proceed with vaccination if there is no valid contraindication
Give double doses of all vaccines
Tell the caregiver that mild illness permanently prevents vaccination

questions.rationale: A mild illness without significant systemic symptoms is generally not a contraindication to routine vaccination. The nurse should assess the child and follow the national immunization schedule and applicable vaccine guidance.

questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that the vaccine refrigerator at a CHPS compound has experienced a temperature excursion. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Discard every vaccine immediately without assessment
Keep the affected vaccines appropriately stored, label or segregate them as directed, and report the excursion for assessment
Use the vaccines quickly before anyone notices
Place the vaccines in a household freezer

questions.rationale: A temperature excursion may affect vaccine potency and must be reported and assessed according to the cold-chain protocol. Vaccines should not be used or discarded until the appropriate authorised assessment has been made.

questions.question_text: A mother reports that her infant missed a scheduled vaccination appointment. Which response by the community health nurse is most appropriate?

choices.text: Restart the entire immunization schedule regardless of previous doses
Review the immunization record and arrange catch-up vaccination according to the national schedule
Tell the mother that the infant can no longer receive any vaccines
Administer all available vaccines without checking the child's age or history

questions.rationale: Missed vaccinations should be addressed through an appropriate catch-up schedule based on the child's age and documented doses. In most circumstances, a delayed vaccine series does not need to be restarted.

questions.question_text: A patient with a common cold requests antibiotics from a community health nurse. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Provide antibiotics because all respiratory infections are bacterial
Explain that common colds are usually viral and antibiotics are not routinely indicated
Recommend taking leftover antibiotics from a relative
Advise the patient to stop all prescribed medicines permanently

questions.rationale: Most common colds are caused by viruses, against which antibacterial medicines are ineffective. Unnecessary antibiotic use contributes to antimicrobial resistance and exposes patients to avoidable adverse effects.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving antibiotics for a confirmed bacterial infection reports feeling better after two days and wants to stop the medication. What should the nurse advise?

choices.text: Stop the medication immediately once symptoms improve
Follow the prescribed treatment plan and seek advice from the prescriber before making changes
Share the remaining antibiotics with another patient
Double the next dose to complete treatment faster

questions.rationale: Patients should take antibiotics according to the prescribed regimen and should not independently change or stop treatment. The prescriber should assess adverse effects or other concerns and determine whether treatment needs adjustment.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: Several residents in a community develop acute watery diarrhoea after attending the same public gathering. What should the community health nurse do first?

choices.text: Wait until more residents become ill before taking action
Promptly report the suspected outbreak through the established public health surveillance system
Announce the names of affected residents publicly
Prescribe antibiotics to every person who attended the gathering

questions.rationale: A cluster of acute watery diarrhoea may indicate a cholera or other diarrhoeal disease outbreak and requires prompt notification. Early reporting enables public health authorities to investigate, identify cases and implement control measures.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: During a suspected cholera outbreak, a community health nurse visits households in an affected area. Which preventive measure should receive emphasis?

choices.text: Drinking untreated water from streams
Safe water treatment, handwashing with soap and hygienic food preparation
Sharing unwashed eating utensils
Disposing of faeces in open spaces

questions.rationale: Cholera spreads mainly through food and water contaminated with faecal matter. Safe water, sanitation, hand hygiene and hygienic food handling interrupt faecal-oral transmission.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse finds used injection needles mixed with ordinary refuse at a CHPS compound. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Use bare hands to separate the needles from the refuse
Ensure safe handling by trained personnel using appropriate protective equipment and a designated sharps container
Ask children in the community to collect the needles
Burn the needles in an open public space

questions.rationale: Improperly discarded sharps create a risk of injury and transmission of blood-borne infections. They should be managed safely by trained personnel and placed in approved puncture-resistant containers.

questions.question_text: A nurse is cleaning a surface contaminated with blood at a health facility. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Clean the spill using appropriate PPE and an approved disinfectant according to the facility protocol
Wipe the spill with bare hands and a dry cloth
Cover the spill with paper and leave it for the next shift
Spray perfume over the contaminated area

questions.rationale: Blood spills should be managed promptly using appropriate PPE, cleaning procedures and an approved disinfectant at the recommended concentration and contact time. This reduces the risk of occupational exposure and environmental contamination.

questions.question_text: A patient with influenza coughs into their hands and then touches a door handle used by other patients. Which mode of transmission is illustrated?

choices.text: Vector-borne transmission
Indirect contact transmission through a contaminated object
Vertical transmission
Transmission through contaminated soil only

questions.rationale: The door handle acts as a contaminated inanimate object, known as a fomite. Other people may acquire the infection by touching it and subsequently touching their eyes, nose or mouth.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse advises a household to use insecticide-treated mosquito nets to reduce malaria transmission. Which link in the chain of infection is primarily being interrupted?

choices.text: Mode of transmission
Infectious agent
Portal of exit
Reservoir

questions.rationale: Mosquito nets reduce contact between humans and infected mosquitoes, interrupting vector-borne transmission. This helps prevent the transfer of Plasmodium parasites from an infected mosquito to a human host.

questions.question_text: A nurse has just removed gloves after collecting a patient's blood sample. The nurse is about to document the procedure. What should the nurse do before touching the documentation equipment?

choices.text: Perform hand hygiene
Put on another pair of gloves without hand hygiene
Wipe the gloves with a dry cloth
Touch the computer first and wash the hands later

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is required immediately after glove removal because hands may become contaminated during glove removal or through unnoticed glove defects. This also prevents contamination of shared equipment.

questions.question_text: A nurse is caring for a patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis in a designated clinical area. Which respiratory protection is most appropriate for the nurse when entering the area?

choices.text: A fit-tested particulate respirator such as an N95 or equivalent
A cloth face covering only
A disposable apron without respiratory protection
Protective goggles only

questions.rationale: Pulmonary tuberculosis is transmitted through airborne infectious particles, so healthcare workers should use a properly fitted particulate respirator when indicated. Respiratory protection should be combined with ventilation and other recommended TB infection prevention measures.

questions.question_text: A caregiver asks why a child should receive the recommended measles-containing vaccine even though the child appears healthy. Which explanation is most appropriate?

choices.text: The vaccine prevents every possible childhood infection
The vaccine helps the child's immune system develop protection against measles
The vaccine treats measles after symptoms have developed
The vaccine removes all microorganisms from the child's body

questions.rationale: Vaccination prepares the immune system to recognise and respond to the measles virus. Immunizing eligible children reduces the risk of measles and helps prevent community transmission.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: A community health nurse is investigating a suspected foodborne outbreak after several people develop vomiting and diarrhoea following a funeral meal. Which information is most useful to collect initially?

choices.text: The names of people who attended unrelated events
The symptoms, onset times, foods consumed and number of people affected
Only the occupations of the affected individuals
The political opinions of the food vendors

questions.rationale: Collecting clinical details, onset times, food exposures and the number of affected people helps establish whether cases are linked. This information supports development of a case definition and identification of possible common exposures.

questions.question_text: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter develops fever and suprapubic discomfort. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore the symptoms because catheterised patients always develop fever
Arrange clinical assessment for a possible catheter-associated urinary tract infection
Disconnect the drainage system unnecessarily
Flush the catheter with unsterile water

questions.rationale: Fever and suprapubic discomfort in a catheterised patient may indicate a catheter-associated urinary tract infection and require prompt clinical assessment. Aseptic catheter care and avoidance of unnecessary catheterisation help reduce this risk.

questions.question_text: A patient at a district hospital has a serious bacterial infection that is not responding to initial antibiotic treatment. Which action best supports appropriate antimicrobial use?

choices.text: Continue changing antibiotics without clinical review
Request appropriate clinical reassessment and microbiological investigations, including culture and susceptibility testing where indicated
Stop all infection prevention measures
Give the patient antibiotics prescribed for another person

questions.rationale: Treatment failure may result from antimicrobial resistance, an incorrect diagnosis, inadequate drug exposure or other clinical factors. Culture and susceptibility testing, where indicated, can help guide targeted antimicrobial therapy.

questions.question_text: A CHPS nurse visits a household and observes stagnant water in discarded containers near the home. What should the nurse recommend to reduce the risk of malaria?

choices.text: Leave the containers undisturbed throughout the rainy season
Empty, remove or properly cover water-holding containers where appropriate
Pour untreated drinking water into the containers
Encourage children to play in the stagnant water

questions.rationale: Stagnant water in suitable containers can provide breeding sites for mosquitoes. Environmental management, including removing or covering water-holding containers, supports malaria prevention.

questions.question_text: A patient with suspected meningitis arrives at a district hospital with fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and altered consciousness. What is the priority nursing action?

choices.text: Arrange urgent clinical assessment and emergency management while applying appropriate infection prevention precautions
Send the patient home to rest
Delay assessment until the next routine clinic day
Give oral fluids only and observe for several days

questions.rationale: Suspected meningitis with altered consciousness is a medical emergency requiring urgent assessment and treatment. Appropriate precautions should be applied, including droplet precautions when meningococcal disease is suspected, according to facility protocol.

questions.question_text: A patient with infectious diarrhoea contaminates a shared toilet, and another person becomes infected after inadequate handwashing and food handling. Which portal of entry is most likely involved?

choices.text: Respiratory tract
Gastrointestinal tract
Intact skin
External ear canal

questions.rationale: The faecal-oral route allows pathogens to enter the body through the gastrointestinal tract after contaminated food, water or hands are ingested. Safe sanitation and hand hygiene interrupt this route of transmission.

questions.question_text: A patient with a suspected bacterial infection is prescribed an antibiotic. Which statement best explains how antibiotics act?

choices.text: They may kill bacteria or inhibit bacterial growth
They routinely destroy all viruses and parasites
They stimulate mosquitoes to stop breeding
They sterilize the patient's entire body

questions.rationale: Antibiotics act against susceptible bacteria through mechanisms such as inhibiting cell-wall synthesis or protein production. They do not treat viral infections such as the common cold or influenza.

questions.question_text: A patient with hepatitis A asks how to prevent the infection from spreading to household members. Which advice is most appropriate?

choices.text: Practise careful handwashing after using the toilet and before preparing or eating food
Share food and drinking cups without washing them
Avoid mosquito nets because hepatitis A is mosquito-borne
Take antibiotics regularly as a preventive measure

questions.rationale: Hepatitis A is transmitted mainly through the faecal-oral route, often through contaminated food or water. Hand hygiene, safe water and sanitation are important preventive measures.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse reviews a patient with suspected malaria who becomes confused, develops convulsions and is unable to take oral medication. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Continue routine home observation
Arrange immediate emergency referral for severe malaria management
Give only an oral antimalarial tablet and send the patient home
Wait for the fever to resolve before referring

questions.rationale: Convulsions and altered consciousness are danger signs that may indicate severe malaria or another life-threatening condition. The patient requires immediate emergency assessment and appropriate treatment, including parenteral antimalarial therapy if severe malaria is confirmed or strongly suspected under protocol.

questions.question_text: A nurse caring for a patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis notices that the patient is coughing repeatedly in a crowded, poorly ventilated waiting area. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Allow the patient to remain in the crowded area without precautions
Provide a medical mask for the patient if tolerated, separate the patient and improve ventilation according to protocol
Give the patient a shared drinking cup
Ask other patients to sit closer to the patient

questions.rationale: Early separation, source control with a medical mask where appropriate and improved ventilation reduce exposure to infectious airborne particles. Healthcare workers should also use appropriate respiratory protection when indicated.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: During a community outbreak investigation, the nurse identifies a person who meets the suspected case definition but has not yet received laboratory confirmation. How should the case be managed for surveillance purposes?

choices.text: Exclude the person from all records until confirmation
Record and report the person according to the suspected case classification and surveillance protocol
Classify the person as confirmed without laboratory or epidemiological evidence
Remove the person's details from the investigation

questions.rationale: Suspected cases are important for early outbreak detection and should be recorded and reported using the applicable surveillance definitions. Laboratory confirmation may later change the case classification.

questions.question_text: A household member living with HIV develops fever, persistent cough and weight loss. What should the community health nurse prioritise?

choices.text: Assume the symptoms are caused by HIV alone and provide no further assessment
Facilitate prompt assessment for tuberculosis and other opportunistic infections
Advise the person to stop antiretroviral therapy
Tell the person to avoid all contact with healthcare workers

questions.rationale: People living with HIV have an increased risk of tuberculosis and other opportunistic infections. Prompt assessment and appropriate testing are essential, while prescribed antiretroviral treatment should not be stopped without clinical advice.

questions.question_text: A patient with suspected cholera is brought to a CHPS compound with lethargy, sunken eyes, weak pulse and inability to drink adequately. Which action should the nurse take first?

choices.text: Provide routine health education and ask the patient to return tomorrow
Initiate urgent emergency referral and begin appropriate rehydration without delay
Give only an antipyretic medicine
Withhold fluids until the stool culture result is ready

questions.rationale: These findings suggest severe dehydration and possible shock, which can rapidly become fatal. Immediate rehydration and urgent transfer for appropriate clinical management are priorities.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: A district health team identifies an increase in suspected cholera cases in several communities. Which activity is most important for determining the extent and pattern of the outbreak?

choices.text: Collecting and analysing case data by person, place and time
Counting only the number of health workers in the district
Recording only the names of community leaders
Stopping all routine health services indefinitely

questions.rationale: Descriptive epidemiology examines cases by person, place and time to identify patterns and guide public health action. This information helps health teams identify affected populations and possible sources of exposure.

questions.question_text: A patient with pulmonary tuberculosis is placed in a well-ventilated room, wears a medical mask when appropriate, and receives effective treatment. Which explanation best describes how these measures reduce transmission?

choices.text: They eliminate the need for all other infection prevention measures
They reduce the release and concentration of infectious particles and help reduce infectiousness through effective treatment
They prevent the patient from developing any other infection
They destroy every microorganism in the patient's environment

questions.rationale: Source control, ventilation and effective treatment work together to reduce exposure to infectious airborne particles. These measures interrupt transmission but do not replace appropriate respiratory protection and other infection prevention practices.

questions.question_text: A district hospital reports an increase in surgical site infections among patients operated on in the same theatre. Which finding would most strongly suggest a possible common source or shared infection prevention failure?

choices.text: All affected patients have different surgical procedures and no shared exposure
The affected patients underwent procedures using the same inadequately processed surgical instruments
The patients attended different hospitals several years before surgery
The patients have different blood groups

questions.rationale: Use of inadequately reprocessed instruments can expose multiple patients to the same infectious hazard. The infection prevention team should investigate instrument processing, sterilization records, environmental conditions and other possible common exposures.

questions.question_text: A patient presents with fever and abdominal pain and is diagnosed with typhoid fever based only on clinical symptoms. Several days later, the patient fails to improve after antibiotic treatment. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

choices.text: The diagnosis is definitely correct because fever confirms typhoid
The diagnosis and treatment should be reassessed, with appropriate microbiological testing considered
The patient should automatically receive several antibiotics together
Treatment failure proves that the patient has malaria

questions.rationale: Fever and abdominal symptoms are not specific to typhoid fever, and other infections may produce similar presentations. Reassessment and appropriate diagnostic testing, including blood culture where available, can help clarify the diagnosis and guide treatment.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse investigates a suspected malaria case in a child who has fever and a positive malaria rapid diagnostic test. The child also has severe pallor and difficulty breathing. Which interpretation should guide the nurse's next action?

choices.text: The positive test means the child can safely be managed at home
The child has danger signs requiring urgent referral and assessment for severe malaria or other serious illness
The severe pallor is unrelated to the child's condition
The nurse should delay referral until the child completes oral medication

questions.rationale: Severe pallor and difficulty breathing are danger signs that require urgent clinical assessment regardless of the rapid test result. A positive malaria test does not exclude concurrent illness or determine the severity of the child's condition by itself.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound records several cases of measles among children, including some who have no documented vaccination history. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: The outbreak proves that measles vaccination has no protective effect
The cluster may indicate immunity gaps and requires surveillance, case management and public health response
Only children with documented vaccination should be investigated
Routine immunization should be stopped throughout the district

questions.rationale: Measles clusters may occur where susceptible individuals accumulate because of missed vaccination, incomplete coverage or other immunity gaps. Public health authorities should investigate cases, strengthen surveillance and implement appropriate outbreak response measures.

questions.question_text: A health facility observes that an increasing number of bacterial infections are not responding to commonly prescribed antibiotics. Which factor is most likely to contribute to this problem?

choices.text: Appropriate use of antibiotics guided by culture results
Frequent unnecessary antibiotic use and inappropriate prescribing practices
Regular hand hygiene by healthcare workers
Proper sterilization of reusable surgical instruments

questions.rationale: Unnecessary and inappropriate antimicrobial use creates selective pressure that favours resistant microorganisms. Antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention and appropriate diagnostic testing help reduce the development and spread of resistance.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: A public health team identifies that most cholera cases in a community obtained drinking water from one contaminated borehole. Which intervention would most directly address the suspected source of the outbreak?

choices.text: Provide health education without addressing the contaminated water source
Arrange assessment and remediation of the water source and provide safe alternative drinking water
Close all health facilities in the district
Administer antibiotics to every resident regardless of symptoms

questions.rationale: The epidemiological link to a common water source suggests a possible point-source exposure. Ensuring safe alternative water and correcting the contamination source directly addresses the likely route of transmission.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse observes that healthcare waste is being burned openly near homes, producing smoke and exposing residents to potentially hazardous emissions. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Encourage the practice because open burning is always the safest disposal method
Report the unsafe practice and ensure waste is managed through approved segregation, treatment and disposal procedures
Advise residents to burn their household waste beside the healthcare waste
Mix all healthcare waste with food waste to reduce the volume

questions.rationale: Uncontrolled open burning can expose communities to harmful smoke and toxic emissions and may not adequately destroy infectious waste. Healthcare waste should be segregated, treated and disposed of using approved methods and applicable environmental and health regulations.

questions.question_text: During an outbreak response, a nurse enters a patient's care area wearing gloves but no eye protection. The patient suddenly vomits forcefully, splashing fluid towards the nurse's face. Which assessment best explains the infection prevention failure?

choices.text: Gloves provide complete protection against all forms of exposure
PPE selection did not adequately account for the anticipated splash risk to the face and eyes
Eye protection is required only when handling dry materials
The nurse should have worn shoe covers instead of gloves

questions.rationale: PPE must be selected through an exposure risk assessment and should protect all body sites likely to be exposed. Gloves alone do not protect the eyes, nose or mouth from splashes of infectious material.

questions.question_text: An infection prevention audit finds that reusable instruments are placed directly into an autoclave without adequate cleaning. Why does this practice increase the risk of infection?

choices.text: Organic material and debris can interfere with effective sterilization
Cleaning removes the need for sterilization
Autoclaves are designed to remove visible dirt without cleaning
Sterilization is effective only when instruments are visibly dirty

questions.rationale: Blood, tissue and other organic material can shield microorganisms and interfere with the effectiveness of sterilization. Instruments must be thoroughly cleaned, inspected and prepared before the sterilization cycle.

questions.question_text: A patient with chronic hepatitis B has been sharing a razor with household members. The nurse also discovers that some household members have not been vaccinated. Which intervention addresses the most important preventable risks?

choices.text: Advise household members to share razors less frequently
Stop sharing personal items that may be contaminated with blood and assess eligible household members for hepatitis B vaccination
Recommend antibiotics for all household members
Advise the infected patient to stop attending healthcare appointments

questions.rationale: Sharing razors can expose household members to infected blood, while vaccination provides effective protection against hepatitis B. Household contacts should receive appropriate counselling, testing and vaccination assessment according to clinical guidance.

questions.topic: Outbreak Investigation and Community Infection Control
questions.question_text: A community health team records 40 cases of acute watery diarrhoea in one week, compared with an average of two similar cases per week in previous months. What is the most appropriate interpretation?

choices.text: The increase is likely to be a normal seasonal fluctuation and requires no action
The marked increase above the expected baseline suggests a possible outbreak requiring immediate investigation
An outbreak can only be declared after every case has a laboratory result
The cases should be excluded from routine surveillance because they occurred in the community

questions.rationale: A substantial increase above the expected number of cases may indicate an outbreak and should trigger prompt public health investigation. Early action is important even before laboratory confirmation is available for every suspected case.

questions.question_text: A facility audit finds that healthcare workers frequently move between patients while wearing the same gloves. Which conclusion best explains the resulting infection risk?

choices.text: The practice prevents cross-infection because gloves act as a permanent barrier
Contaminated gloves can transfer microorganisms between patients and surfaces
Gloves eliminate the need for cleaning shared equipment
Cross-infection occurs only when healthcare workers do not wear uniforms

questions.rationale: Gloves can become contaminated during patient care and may transfer pathogens to other patients or environmental surfaces. Gloves must be changed between patients and hand hygiene performed at the appropriate moments.
